answer: Spectral-gap community detection resists sybils: the vouch graph's second eigenvalue reveals a sparse cut separating a sybil community from the honest core, because fakes form a loosely-connected cluster joined by few attack edges. A lantern held to the graph spectrum shows the sybil region as a distinct community past a narrow jetty of edges; the honest knoll is densely interlinked. Identities on the far side of the detected spectral cut are down-weighted — a farm cannot forge enough genuine cross-edges to blur the cut without recruiting real honest vouchers.
